patients.label: 15-year-old male sea swimmer with chronic suppurative otitis media from which Achromobacter spp. and V. parahaemolyticus were isolated

identity_evidence.quote: A 15-year-old male, a sea swimmer, presented with persistent otorrhea and hearing impairment

attribution_limitations: The authors speculate that V. parahaemolyticus is plausibly linked to seawater exposure and that Achromobacter spp. may be an opportunistic colonizer favored by prior antibiotic courses; the case report does not establish the source or the pathogenic role of either organism.
MALDI-TOF MS identified the Achromobacter isolate as A. xylosoxidans, but the authors report it as Achromobacter spp. because the method cannot reliably discriminate closely related species.
Table 1 shows dashes for swab 2 (anaerobic culture) and swab 3 (fungal culture) organism, identification, susceptibility method and results; no anaerobic or fungal result is stated in the text.
Table 1 lists the swab 1 susceptibilities (carbapenems; fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines) in one cell without naming the organism; the organism assignment comes from the text.

limitations: No figures or supplements are listed in the source.
Table 1 swab 2 and swab 3 cells are dashes; recorded as not reported, not as negative results.
The case text gives no dates, culture timing relative to presentation, or susceptibility values (MICs); treatment sequence is ordered only where the text states it.

claims.text: Otoscopy showed tympanic membrane perforation with purulent discharge. Ear discharge was collected with three swabs; aerobic culture grew a mixed culture of Achromobacter spp. and V. parahaemolyticus identified by MALDI-TOF MS. On VITEK 2 testing the Achromobacter spp. isolate was multidrug resistant and susceptible only to carbapenems, and V. parahaemolyticus was susceptible to fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines. Table 1 lists no results for the anaerobic and fungal swabs.
